akhfash:2-3.t: He said ﴿لاَ أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ ﴿وَلاَ أَنتُمْ عَابِدُونَ﴾: because ﴿لا﴾ runs the course of ﴿ما﴾, it was made nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject).

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿لَا أَعْبُدُ﴾ in the present ﴿مَا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ of idols,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَلَا أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ﴾ in the present ﴿مَا أَعْبُدُ﴾, which is Allah the Exalted alone,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَلَا أَنَا عَابِدٌ﴾ in the future ﴿مَا عَبَدْتُمْ﴾

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَلَا أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ﴾ in the future ﴿مَا أَعْبُدُ﴾: Allah knew of them that they would not believe. Applying «ما» to Allah is by way of correspondence (muqābala).

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ﴾: associating partners ﴿وَلِيَ دِينِ﴾: Islam. This was before he was commanded to fight. The Seven [readers] drop the yāʾ of the possessive (yāʾ al-iḍāfa) in pausing and in continuous reading, and Yaʿqūb retains it in both cases.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿يا﴾ a vocative particle. ﴿أي﴾ the one addressed (munādā), a specified indefinite (nakira maqṣūda). ﴿ها﴾ for drawing attention (tanbīh). ﴿الْكافِرُونَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) or a badal (substitute); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿لا أَعْبُدُ﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿لا﴾ is negative. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عابِدُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle (ism al-fāʿil). ﴿أَعْبُدُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿لا﴾ is negative. ﴿أَنا عابِدٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿عَبَدْتُّمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ﴾ لكم is a fronted khabar (predicate) and دينكم a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلِيَ دِينِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it.

dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ يا أَيُّهَا الْكافِرُونَ) A group of the polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Come, worship what we worship and we will worship what you worship, and let us share, you and we, in all of our affair. If what you have brought is better than what we have, we will have shared you in it and taken our portion of it; and if what we have is better than what you have, you will have shared us in our affair and taken your portion of it." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent this surah down. قل is an imperative verb, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; يا is a vocative particle for a mid-range addressee; أي is the one addressed, an indefinite specified noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative; ها is for alerting; and الكافرون is a badal (substitute) for أي or a naʿt (adjective) of it. Ibn Khālawayh said: "If someone asks and says: the alerting particle enters before the vague noun, as in هذا, so why did it enter here after أي? Then say: because أيّ is annexed to what follows it, and had the alerting particle not separated الكافرين from أيّ, the mind would have gone to the idea that it is in a genitive construct." (لا أَعْبُدُ ما تَعْبُدُونَ)
لا is a negative particle; أعبد is an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; and ما is a relative (mawṣūl) meaning "that which" (الذي), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause تعبدون is its ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "you worship it". It is also permissible that it be maṣdariyya (a verbal-noun-forming ما), so that together with what follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) serving as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (وَلا أَنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أَعْبُدُ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; أنتم is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and عابدون the khabar (predicate); and ما is a relative noun, used for rational beings by way of exaltation, a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause أعبد is the ṣila. Or ما is maṣdariyya, so that it, with what lies within its scope, is a mafʿūl muṭlaq. (وَلا أَنا عابِدٌ ما عَبَدْتُّمْ وَلا أَنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أَعْبُدُ) This is likewise a conjunction. What the i'rab scholars have reported about ما comes down to this: it means "that which". If what is meant by it is the idols, as in the first and third, the matter is clear, because they are not rational beings, and ما in origin is for non-rational beings. And if what is meant by it is the Creator, Exalted is He, as in the second and fourth, then whoever permits its use for those possessed of knowledge takes this as evidence, while whoever forbids it makes it maṣdariyya, the implied form being "nor are you worshippers of my worship". Abū Muslim said: "The ما in the first two means 'those whom' (الذين), the intended sense being the object of worship, and the ما in the last two is maṣdariyya, meaning: I do not worship as you worship, a worship built on doubt and neglect of reflection, and you do not worship like my worship, which is built on certainty." From all of this three views result: 1- that they are all "that which"; 2- that they are all maṣdariyya; 3- or the first two are "that which" and the last two maṣdariyya. And one might say: it would be good if the first and third were taken as "that which" and the second and fourth as maṣdariyya, so that ما need not be used of those possessed of knowledge. The meaning of the repetition will come in the section on rhetoric. (لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِيَ دِينِ) لكم is a fronted khabar and دينكم a postponed mubtadaʾ; ولي دين is conjoined to what precedes.

* Rhetoric:
The scholars of rhetoric and grammar differed: is the repetition in this surah for emphasis or not, and if it is not for emphasis, by what means did the difference come about so that emphasis is excluded? We shall set out their views, with a necessary brief indication of each.
1- A group said: the repetition is for emphasis. His words "nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped" are an emphasis of His words "I do not worship what you worship", and His words "nor are you worshippers of what I worship" are an emphasis of His words "nor are you worshippers of what I worship"; and likewise: "Which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?", "Woe on that Day to the deniers", "No! You will soon know, then no! You will soon know", and "No! They will soon know, then no! They will soon know". The benefit of this emphasis here is to cut off the hopes of the disbelievers and to confirm the report that they will meet their end in disbelief and will never submit.
[Translator's note: the second example in item 1 is written identically to the clause it is said to emphasise, as in the source; the second clause was presumably meant to differ, e.g. "ولا أنا عابد ما عبدتم" being emphasised by "ولا أنتم عابدون ما أعبد".]
2- A group said: the repetition is not for emphasis. al-Akhfash said: "'I do not worship now what you worship, nor are you now worshippers of what I worship, nor am I in the future a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor are you in the future worshippers of what I worship.' So emphasis is removed and a new establishing statement results, since each clause is restricted to a time other than the time of the other." There is something to examine in this view: how could the Messenger of Allah ﷺ restrict his negation of worshipping what they worship? This is not sound.
3- Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Since his words 'I do not worship' could be taken to mean 'now', leaving the future awaiting what will occur in it, the clarification came in His words 'nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped', i.e. ever; then came His second words 'nor are you worshippers of what I worship', making it certain for them that they will never believe. This is the meaning of the back-and-forth in this surah; it is of superb eloquence and is not mere repetition, but contains what I have mentioned."
4- al-Zamakhsharī said: "'I do not worship' is meant for worship in the future, because لا enters only on an imperfect verb with a future sense, just as ما enters only on an imperfect verb with a present sense. The meaning is: I will not do in the future what you ask of me, namely worshipping your gods, and you will not do in it what I ask of you, namely worshipping my God. 'Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped' means: I never at all worshipped in the past what you worshipped in it, that is, no worship of an idol was ever known from me in the Jāhiliyya, so how could it be hoped for from me in Islam? 'Nor are you worshippers of what I worship' means: and you did not worship, at any time, what I am now devoted to worshipping."
5- Abū Ḥayyān said: "What I choose regarding these clauses is that He negated his worship in the future, since the usual function of لا is to negate the future; then He conjoined to it 'nor are you worshippers of what I worship', a negation of the future by way of correspondence. Then He said 'nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped', a negation of the present, because the real force of the operating active participle is indication of the present; then He conjoined to it 'nor are you worshippers of what I worship', a negation of the present by way of correspondence. So the meaning is ordered thus: he, upon him be peace, does not worship what they worship, neither now nor in the future, and they likewise, as Allah has sealed their end upon disbelief. When He said 'I do not worship what you worship' and applied ما to the idols, He matched the speech with ما in 'what I worship', even though what is meant by it is Allah the Exalted, because in correspondence what is not allowed in isolation is allowed. This is according to the school of those who say that ما is not used for individual persons of knowledge; as for whoever allows that, namely Sībawayh, he has no need for the excuse of correspondence."
6- al-Qurṭubī said: "It was also said that this, i.e. the repetition, matches their words: 'You worship our gods and we worship your God, then you worship our gods and we worship your God, and we carry on thus always, a year and a year.' So they were answered on everything they said with its opposite, i.e. this will never be. Ibn ʿAbbās said: the Quraysh said to the Prophet ﷺ: 'We will give you wealth until you are the richest man in Mecca, and we will marry you to whom you wish, and we will tread on your heel,' i.e. walk behind you, 'if you stop insulting our gods. If you will not, then we offer you one proposal, which is good for us and for you: you worship our gods al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā for a year and we worship your God for a year, then you worship our gods and we worship your God, and we carry on thus always, a year and a year.' So the surah was sent down, and the repetition in 'I do not worship what you worship' is because the people repeated their statement time after time."
7- Ibn al-Athīr said in his book al-Mathal al-Sāʾir: "Some people thought this verse to be a repetition with no benefit, and it is not so. For the meaning of 'I do not worship' is: in the future, of worshipping your gods, and you will not do in it what I ask of you, namely worshipping my God; 'nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped' means: I never at all worshipped in the past what you worshipped in it, i.e. no worship of an idol was known from me in the Jāhiliyya at any time, so how could that be hoped for from me in Islam; 'nor are you worshippers', in the past at any time, 'of what I am now devoted to worshipping'." This is a repetition of what al-Zamakhsharī said, word for word and verbatim.
8- Ibn Khālawayh said: "If someone asks and says: what is the reason for the repetition in this surah? Then say: its meaning is that some of the disbelievers of Quraysh came to the Prophet and said: 'You are the master of Banū Hāshim and the son of their masters, and you should not deride the sensibilities of your people; rather, we will worship your Lord for a year and you worship our gods for a year.' So there was sent down 'Say: O disbelievers...' to the end. If someone says: some of them did become Muslim after that time, so why was it said 'nor are you worshippers'? The answer is that this was sent down regarding particular people who died in disbelief, and Allah the Exalted knew that of them, so He reported that they would never believe, as He said: 'It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they do not believe', regarding particular people, while the admonition did benefit other people. There is another answer in it: that the address is general but meant specifically, for those who do not believe, even though among them were some who had believed."

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾.
They said to al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ: Tell your nephew to touch one of our idols, and we will follow him. Al-ʿAbbās told him that, and the Prophet ﷺ, came to them while they were sitting in a circle and recited this surah to them; so they despaired of him and harmed him. This was before he was commanded to fight them. Then He said: ﴿لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ﴾: unbelief, ﴿وَلِىَ دِينِ﴾ (6): Islam. He did not say «ديني», because the verses [end] in nūn, so the yāʾ was dropped, as He said: ﴿فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ، والّذِى هُوَ يُطْعِمُنِى وَيَسْقِينِ﴾.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: (لا أعبد ما تعبدون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the answer to the vocative, resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «ولا أنتم عابدون» is conjoined to the answer to the vocative; «ما»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «عابدون».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: (لكم دينكم ولي دين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, Exalted is He (الكافرون): a naʿt (adjective) of (أيّ); its omission is not permissible, because it is the one addressed (al-munādā) in meaning. According to most grammarians its being accusative is not permissible, as is permissible in «يا زيد الظريفَ» in the accusative, as a naʿt following the position of (زيد), since it is in the position of the accusative by the vocative. Its explanation has already passed.
(ما) in the four places is in the position of the accusative by the verb before each of them, and it has the meaning of (الذي); the hāʾ is omitted from the verb after each of them, i.e. «تعبدونه», «أعبده» and «عبدتموه». And it was said: (ما) together with the verb is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so on this view there is no need to imply an omission.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is a negative particle.
﴿أنا﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿عابد﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle ﴿عابد﴾; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "nor am I a worshipper of that which you worshipped". Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "nor am I a worshipper [with] your worship".
﴿عبدتم﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn; the tāʾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent), and the mīm is the sign of the plural. The clause ﴿عبدتم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position; the clause ﴿ولا أنا عابد﴾ has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the response of the vocative.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is a negative particle.
﴿أنتم﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿عابدون﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural.
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle ﴿عابدون﴾; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "nor are you worshippers of that which I worship". Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "nor are you worshippers [with] my worship".
﴿أعبد﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the ḍamma; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنا". The clause ﴿أعبد﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position; the clause ﴿ولا أنتم عابدون﴾ has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the response of the vocative.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿لكم﴾: the lām is a preposition, and the pronoun attached to it is in the position of the genitive (majrūr); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of ﴿دينكم﴾.
﴿دينكم﴾: a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and it is muḍāf; the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the mīm is the sign of the plural. The clause ﴿لكم دينكم﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya) and has no grammatical position.
﴿ولي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ولي: the lām is a preposition, and the pronoun attached to it is in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted, fronted khabar of ﴿دين﴾.
﴿دين﴾: a delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the letter before the omitted yāʾ of the first person; the omitted yāʾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. The clause ﴿ولي دين﴾ has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ﴿لكم دينكم﴾.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿قل﴾: an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and its agent is necessarily latent (mustatir) in it, its implied form being "you" (أنت); the clause ﴿قل﴾ is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.
﴿يا﴾: a vocative particle.
﴿أيها﴾: «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative, and ﴿ها﴾ is for alerting.
﴿الكافرون﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾; the clause ﴿يا أيها الكافرون﴾ is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of accusative.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿أعبد﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "I" (أنا).
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "I do not worship that which you worship" (لا أعبد الذي تعبدونه). Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "I do not worship with your worship" (لا أعبد عبادتكم).
﴿تعبدون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs, and ﴿واو الجماعة﴾ (the wāw of the plural) is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿تعبدون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿لا أعبد...﴾ is the answer to the vocative, resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and «لا» is negating.
﴿أنتم﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿عابدون﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the wāw, because it is a sound masculine plural.
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle ﴿عابدون﴾, and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "nor are you worshippers of what I worship" (ولا أنتم عابدون الذي أعبده). Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "nor are you worshipping with my worship" (ولا أنتم عابدون عبادتي).
﴿أعبد﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the ḍamma, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "I" (أنا); the clause ﴿أعبد﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿ولا أنتم عابدون﴾ has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the answer to the vocative.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: قُلْ is in the position of the jussive (jazm) according to al-Farrāʾ, on the basis of the omission of the lām. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: if it were as he said, it would be with tāʾ (i.e., لِتقل). According to the Basrans it is not declinable. يا أَيُّهَا: «يا» is a vocative particle, and you give أيّ ḍamma because it is a singular vocative; the reason for this has already been given. الْكافِرُونَ is a naʿt (adjective) of أيّ, or a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: there is no repetition in this; only one ignorant of the language says that it is repeated. And the meaning is: قُلْ يا أَيُّهَا الْكافِرُونَ (1).

nahhas-irab:2-5.t:
لا أَعْبُدُ ما تَعْبُدُونَ (2) at this time, and likewise وَلا أَنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أَعْبُدُ (3); this is concluded. Then He said: وَلا أَنا عابِدٌ ما عَبَدْتُّمْ (4) in what is to come, and وَلا أَنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أَعْبُدُ (5) likewise. In this there was an indication of his prophethood ﷺ, because of all those whom he addressed with this address, not one of them then embraced Islam; and likewise those whom He addressed with His saying سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ [al-Baqara: 6].
أَنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise أَنا عابِدٌ, with the wāw omitted [Translator's note: so in the text], and its meaning. «لا» does not put (the predicate) in the accusative as «ما» does, because «ما» enters more deeply into resemblance to ليس, so it governs the accusative as ليس does.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ: (دينكم is) a mubtadaʾ (subject), and likewise وَلِيَ دِينِ. The yāʾ was dropped from ديني because it is the end of a verse, so the dropping was good so that the verse-endings agree. Whoever gives the yāʾ fatḥa in «ولي» says: it is a noun (pronoun), and I disliked to impair it; and whoever makes it quiescent says: it has rested on what precedes it, in the position of the accusative [Translator's note: so in the text].

safi-cedvel:1-6.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) is an indefinite specific vocative, indeclinable on ḍamma in the position of accusative. (الكافرون) is a badal of أيّ – or ʿaṭf bayān to it – following it in the nominative in form. (لا) is negative. (ما) is a relative [Note: or an indefinite noun with a description.. or a maṣdar particle with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e.: I do not worship as you worship, a worship built on doubt.] in the position of accusative, a direct object, and the returning pronoun is omitted..
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is inceptive.
And the clause: «النداء ... » is in the position of accusative, the thing said (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «لا أعبد ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «تعبدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما).
3- (the wāw) is a conjunction. The second (لا) is a negative, inoperative. (ما) is a relative [Note: this according to those who allow ما to refer to those with knowledge.. or it is a maṣdar particle, the interpreted maṣdar being a direct object.] in the position of accusative, a direct object..
And the clause: «لا أنتم عابدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «أعبد ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
4-6 (لا أنا ... عبدتم) is like لا أنتم ... أعبد, repeated a second time. (لكم) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (دينكم), (لي) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (دين), which is nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ, which was dropped for lightness.
And the clause: «لا أنا عابد ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «عبدتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the third relative (ما).
And the clause: «لا أنتم عابدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «أعبد ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the fourth relative (ما).
And the clause: «لكم دينكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
And the clause: «لي دين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the causal clause.

* Rhetoric:
Repetition (takrār): in the noble verses, for emphasis. His saying, the Exalted, «وَلا أَنا عابِدٌ ما عَبَدْتُّمْ» is an emphasis of His saying «لا أَعْبُدُ ما تَعْبُدُونَ», and His saying «وَلا أَنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أَعْبُدُ» is an emphasis of His saying «وَلا أَنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أَعْبُدُ» [Translator's note: the source gives the same verse on both sides of this statement; translated as written] – and the Qur'an was revealed in the language of the Arabs, and it is their custom to repeat speech for emphasis and to make understood: the one who answers affirmatively says "yes, yes", and the one who refuses says "no, no". On this is His saying, the Exalted, «كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ».

* Benefits:
- «لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِيَ دِينِ»:
This sūra was revealed concerning a group of the Quraysh, among them al-Ḥārith ibn Qays al-Sahmī, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and Umayya ibn Khalaf. They said: O Muḥammad, come, follow our religion and we will follow yours, and we will make you a partner in all of our religion: you worship our gods for a year and we worship your God for a year. If what you have brought is better, we will have shared in it and taken our portion of it; and if what we have is better, you will have shared with us in our affair and taken your portion of it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Allah forbid that I associate anything else with Him. They said: Then touch some of our gods and we will believe you and worship your God. He said: Until I see what comes from my Lord. So Allah revealed this sūra. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the Sanctuary, where these people were, and recited the sūra over their heads; at that they despaired of him and harmed him together with his Companions.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
[His saying]: {لاَ أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ}: «ما» in this sūra admits two views. The first: that it has the meaning of «الذي». If the idols are meant, as in the first and the third, the matter is clear, because they are not rational beings, and «ما» in origin is for non-rational beings. If the Creator, the Exalted, is meant by it, as in the second and the fourth, then those who allow it to apply to those possessed of knowledge cite it as evidence; and those who disallow it make it a maṣdar (maṣdariyya). The implied form is: "and you are not worshippers of my worship", that is, "the like of my worship". Abū Muslim said: «ما» in the first two has the meaning of «الذي», and what is intended is the object of worship; and «ما» in the last two is a maṣdar, that is: "I do not worship your worship, which is built on doubt and neglect of reflection, and you do not worship the like of my worship, which is built on certainty." From the sum of this three views result: that all of them mean «الذي», or that all are maṣdars, or that the first two mean «الذي» and the last two are maṣdars. And someone could say: if it were said that the first and the third mean «الذي», and the second and the fourth are maṣdars, it would be good, so that «ما» need not apply to those possessed of knowledge, which is what is required by the view of those who disallow its application to those possessed of knowledge, as stated before.
People differed: is the repetition in this sūra for emphasis or not? And if it is not for emphasis, by what means does the distinction come about so that emphasis is excluded? It is necessary to cite their views on this. A group said: it is for emphasis. So His saying {وَلاَ أَنَآ عَابِدٌ مَّا عَبَدتُّمْ} is an emphasis of His saying {لاَ أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ}, and His saying {وَلاَ أَنتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَآ أَعْبُدُ} the second time is an emphasis of {وَلاَ أَنتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَآ أَعْبُدُ} the first time. Like it is His saying {فَبِأَيِّ آلاء رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ} [al-Raḥmān: 13] and {وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ} [al-Mursalāt: 15] in their two sūras, and {كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ} [al-Takāthur: 3-4] and {كَلاَّ سَيَعْلَمُونَ ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سَيَعْلَمُونَ} [al-Nabaʾ: 4-5]. And in the hadith: "I do not permit, then I do not permit; Fāṭima is only a part of me." The poet said:
4663 - هَلاَّ سَأَلْتَ جنودَ كِنْ ... دَةَ يومَ وَلَّوْا أين أَيْنا
(Why did you not ask the troops of Kinda, the day they turned back: where, where to?)
Another said:
4664 - يا علقمَهْ يا عَلْقَمَهْ يا علقَمَهْ ... خيرَ تميمٍ كلِّها وأكرمَهْ
(O ʿAlqama, O ʿAlqama, O ʿAlqama, best of all Tamīm and the most noble!)
Another said:
4665 - يا أقرعُ بنَ حابسٍ يا أقرعُ ... إنك إن يُصْرَعْ أخوكَ تُصْرَعُ
(O Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis, O Aqraʿ, if your brother is thrown down, you will be thrown down.)
Another said:
4666 - ألا يا اسْلَمي ثُمَّ اسْلَمي ثُمَّتَ اسْلَمي ... ثلاثُ تحيَّاتٍ وإن لم تَكَلَّمِ
(Ah, be safe, then be safe, then again be safe: three greetings, though you do not speak.)
Another said:
4667 - يا لَبَكْرٍ أَنْشِرُوا لي كُلَيْباً ... يا لَبَكْرٍ أينَ أينَ الفِرارُ
(O Bakr, raise Kulayb for me! O Bakr, where, where is the flight?)
They said: the Qurʾān came in the manners of the speech of the Arabs. The benefit of the emphasis here is to cut off the hopes of the disbelievers and to confirm the report that they will meet their end in disbelief and that they will never become Muslim.
A group said: it is not for emphasis. Al-Akhfash said: "I do not worship at this moment what you worship, and you are not worshippers this year of what I worship; and I am not a worshipper in the future of what you worshipped, and you are not worshippers in the future of what I worship; so emphasis disappears, since each sentence is bound to a time other than the time of the other." End of quotation.
There is room for objection in it: how can the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bind the denial of his worship of what they worship to a time? This is not sound. And in the reports of the occasions of revelation: they asked him to worship their gods for a year and they would worship his God for a year, and it was revealed; so how can this stand? Abū Muslim made the distinction by what I have reported from him: namely, «ما» in the first two being «الذي» and in the last two a maṣdar. There is room for objection in this too, in that the repetition is in the meaning, and that exists however you imply «ما». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Since His saying «لا أَعْبُدُ» could be meant for the present moment, leaving the future awaiting what will happen in it, the clarification came with His saying {وَلاَ أَنَآ عَابِدٌ مَّا عَبَدتُّمْ}, that is, forever and as long as I live; then came His saying {وَلاَ أَنتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَآ أَعْبُدُ} the second time as a decree upon them that they will never believe, like one who unveils the unseen, as was said to Noah, peace be upon him: {أَنَّهُ لَن يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إِلاَّ مَن قَدْ آمَنَ} [Hūd: 36]. This is the meaning of the reiteration in this sūra, and it is of consummate eloquence, and not mere repetition; rather it has what I have mentioned."
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«لا أعبدُ» is meant for worship in the future, because «لا» enters only on an imperfect in the sense of the future, just as «ما» enters only on an imperfect in the sense of the present. The meaning is: 'I will not do in the future what you ask of me, the worship of your gods, and you will not do in it what I ask of you, the worship of my God; and I am not a worshipper of what you worshipped', that is, 'I never was in the past a worshipper of what you worshipped in it', meaning that worship of an idol was never known of me in the Jāhiliyya, so how could it be hoped of me in Islam? 'And you are not worshippers of what I worship', that is, 'you did not worship at a time what I am engaged in worshipping'. If you ask: why was it not said «ما عبدتُ» as it was said «ما عبدتُمْ»? I say: because they used to worship idols before the mission, and he did not worship Allah the Exalted at that time. If you ask: why did it come with «ما» and not «مَنْ»? I say: because the attribute is meant, as if it had been said: 'I do not worship the false, and you do not worship the true.' It was also said that «ما» is a maṣdar, that is: 'I do not worship your worship, and you do not worship my worship.'" End of quotation. By his saying "because the attribute is meant" he means that the descriptive sense is intended by «ما»; I have already given the verification of this recently in Sūrat «والشمس وضحاها», together with the Shaykh's objection to him and the answer to it, and its origin is in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ at His saying {فانكحوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ النسآء} [al-Nisāʾ: 3].
The Shaykh disputed with him here, saying: "As for his restriction in his saying 'because «لا» enters only', to the end, and in his saying 'just as «ما» enters only', to the end: it is not sound; rather, that is the usual case with them, not an obligatory one. The grammarians have mentioned «لا» entering on the imperfect with the sense of the present, and «ما» entering on the imperfect with the sense of the future. That is mentioned in the extended books of grammar. For this reason Sībawayh did not state it with a particle of restriction; he said only: «لا» is the negation of his saying 'he will do' when the act has not occurred; and he said: 'As for «ما», it is the negation of his saying 'he is doing', when he is in the state of doing.' So he mentioned the usual case in both. As for his saying, on His saying {وَلاَ أَنَآ عَابِدٌ مَّا عَبَدتُّمْ}, 'that is, I never was in the past a worshipper of what you worshipped in it', it does not stand, because ʿābid is an active participle that has governed «ما عَبَدْتُمْ», so it is not explained by the past; it is explained only by the present or the future. His position on the active participle is not the position of al-Kisāʾī and Hishām in allowing its governing in the past. As for his saying 'and you are not worshippers of what I worship', that is, 'you did not worship at a time what I am engaged in worshipping', ʿābidūn has governed «ما أعبد», so it is not explained by the past. As for his saying 'and he did not', to the end, it is bad manners toward the station of prophethood, and it is not correct, because he ﷺ never ceased to be a monotheist to Allah the Exalted, keeping Him exalted above all that does not befit His majesty, avoiding their idols, standing at the sacred sites of his father Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, and performing the pilgrimage to the House; and this is worship, and what worship is greater than the oneness of Allah the Exalted and casting off their idols? The knowledge of Allah the Exalted is the greatest of acts of worship. The Exalted said {وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الجن والإنس إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُونِ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 56]. The commentators said: 'except to know Me', so they called knowledge of Allah the Exalted worship." End of what he disputed with him and his rejection of him.
It may be answered about the first that he built his position on the usual case, and for this reason he brought the restriction; as for what he related from Sībawayh, its apparent sense is with him until evidence stands for something else. And about his making the active participle govern while explaining it by the past, that it is by way of the narration of the present state (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl), as in the saying of the Exalted {وَكَلْبُهُمْ بَاسِطٌ ذِرَاعَيْهِ} [al-Kahf: 18] and His saying {والله مُخْرِجٌ مَّا كُنْتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ} [al-Baqara: 72] and the like.
As for his saying "he was a monotheist, keeping Allah exalted", it is conceded. And his saying "and this is the greatest of acts of worship" is also conceded. But what is meant in the verse is a particular worship, namely the particular prayer, because it is set against what the polytheists did of prostrating to their idols and praying to them; so he ﷺ set against this his prayer to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. But the denial in al-Zamakhsharī's words conveys that he ﷺ was not engaged in worship before the mission, and that is a view very weak and of no account, because the sound hadiths refute it, namely: he used to practise taḥannuth, he used to worship, he used to fast, he used to circumambulate, he used to stand; and none said otherwise except an odd few of the people. In sum, the question is disputed. And if he was engaged in worship, by which law was he worshipping? It was said: by the law of Noah; it was said: Ibrāhīm; it was said: Moses; it was said: Jesus; the evidences for these are in the principles of jurisprudence (uṣūl), so we shall not go into them.
Then the Shaykh said: "What I prefer in these sentences is that he denied his worship in the future, because the usual case with «لا» is that it negates the future; then he conjoined to it {وَلاَ أَنتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَآ أَعْبُدُ}, a negation of the future, by way of antithesis (muqābala). Then He said {وَلاَ أَنَآ عَابِدٌ مَّا عَبَدتُّمْ}, a negation of the present, because the active participle that governs has in reality an indication of the present; then he conjoined to it {وَلاَ أَنتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَآ أَعْبُدُ}, a negation of the present, by way of antithesis. So the meaning is ordered: that he, peace be upon him, does not worship what they worship, in the present or in the future; and they are likewise, since Allah the Exalted decreed their meeting their end in disbelief. When He said 'I do not worship what you worship', applying «ما» to the idols, He set the speech against it with «ما» in His saying 'what I worship', even though what is meant by it is Allah the Exalted, because in antithesis what is allowed is not allowed in isolation. This is on the view of those who say that «ما» does not apply to individuals possessed of knowledge. As for those who allow that, and it is the position of Sībawayh, they have no need to seek an excuse in antithesis."

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِيَ دِينِ}. He brought these two affirmative clauses after negated clauses because, since what mattered most was his (peace be upon him) disassociation from their religion, he began in the preceding clauses with negation of what is attributed to him. Then, once the negation was established, he returned to addressing them with His words {لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِيَ دِينِ}, as a truce with them; then that was abrogated by the command to fight.

Nāfiʿ, Hishām, Ḥafṣ and al-Bazzī (with a disagreement reported from him) read the yāʾ of «لي» with fatḥa, and the rest gave it sukūn. The seven and the majority of the readers omitted the yāʾ of the first person (yāʾ al-iḍāfa) from «ديني», both in pause and in continuation; Sallām and Yaʿqūb kept it in both cases. Its matter is clear from what has preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ (١) لَا أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ (٢)).
The words of the Exalted (مَا تَعْبُدُونَ): «مَا» may be in the sense of «الَّذِي» (that which), with the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) omitted; or it may be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), with nothing omitted, the implied form being: «لَا أَعْبُدُ مِثْلَ عِبَادَتِكُمْ» (I do not worship as you worship). And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-4.t:
Sūrat al-Kāfirūn
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ يا أيُّها الكافِرُونَ﴾ ﴿لا أعْبُدُ ما تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ ﴿وَلا أنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أعْبُدُ﴾ ﴿وَلا أنا عابِدٌ ما عَبَدْتُمْ﴾ ("Say: O unbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshippers of what I worship, nor will I be a worshipper of what you have worshipped"): that is, I am not, in this present state of mine, worshipping what you worship, nor are you worshipping what I worship; and I am not a worshipper of what you have worshipped, that is, nor will I worship in what I face [of the future] what you have worshipped, nor will you, in what you face [of the future], be worshippers of what I worship. So this is a negation of the present, and also that it should be in the future, passing on from the present. And likewise He negated their worship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, in the present and in the future. This — and Allah knows best — concerns his people: Allah let him know that they would not believe, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said in the story of Noah: ﴿لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إلا مَن قَدْ آمَنَ﴾ [Hūd: 36] ("none of your people will believe except those who have already believed").

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿لَكم دِينُكم ولِيَ دِينِ﴾ ("to you your religion and to me mine"): it was said: this was before he ﷺ was commanded to fight.
